item.subject: science
item.stem:
In her school laboratory, Meera mixes lime water (a base) with dilute lemon juice (an acid). She adds the lime water slowly, testing with blue and red litmus paper, until neither paper changes colour.

Which statement best explains what has happened at this point?

options.A: Any amount of lime water will always neutralise any amount of lemon juice, so the solution is neutral straight away.
options.B: Just enough base has been added to react completely with the acid, forming a salt and water, so the solution is neither acidic nor basic.
options.C: The mixture is neutral, so it must contain equal volumes of the acid and the base.
options.D: The blue litmus paper did not change colour, so the solution is still acidic.
